column4: Moses identifies the Lord as the one who أَعْطَىٰ every thing its created form and then guided it, joining bestowed fitness to bestowed direction.
God creates and proportions, supplying the creaturely fitness presupposed by an animal able to bear and move well.
God determines and guides, completing 87:2's fitted creature with direction rather than leaving movement self-generated.
The direction of the way belongs to God while some ways deviate, and He could have guided everyone; the road and its guidance are under His authority.
Moses is commanded to make a dry path through the sea and told not to fear pursuit or dread, a divinely opened and protected route through dangerous terrain.
Livestock are God's provision over which His name is remembered, while humans are told to submit to the one God; animal gift and human yielding meet directly.
The people stood at the brink of a pit of fire and God rescued them from it, combining dangerous footing, imminent fall, and deliverance by another.
Whoever has punishment diverted from him on that Day has received God's mercy, a direct nonlexical counterpart to being made to pass away from fire.
God could send a sign before which their necks remain bowed, making human submission visible in the same bodily point as the mount turning toward its rider.
Every soul comes with a driver and a witness, making externally directed passage into the judgment scene explicit.
People rush toward the summoner while the disbelievers call it a difficult day, joining compelled movement with the Qur'anic ʿusr outcome.
The false assumption about God أَرْدَىٰ its holders, using the section's falling-ruin root for the belief that brings them to loss.
Those who deny the meeting with God carry their burdens upon their backs, reversing the beneficial bearer into a person crushed by his own load.
Disbelievers invite others to follow their way and promise to carry their sins, but the ayah denies that they can bear any of them.
They will bear their own burdens and burdens added to them, exposing the deceptive offer of an easy follower's road in the preceding ayah.
Those fleeing the reminder are likened to startled donkeys, a vivid animal reversal of the calm, quickly following mount.
The donkeys flee from a lion, specifying the uncontrolled fear that drives the contrary animal gait in 74:50.
People who will not hear or understand are compared to livestock and said to be further astray from the way, opposing the animal guided along its route.
The donkey carrying books bears a load without receiving its meaning, setting a limit on what faithful carrying and following amount to.
Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are described as worst in place and furthest astray from the way, reversing upright safe-leading on a road.
Criminals are dragged on their faces into the Fire, the coercive and ruinous opposite of being led safely beside it.
The false gods and the erring are toppled headlong into Hell, giving misdirection the falling end anticipated by the section.
On the day people turn their backs fleeing, no protector from God exists, and one He lets stray has no guide; protection and direction both reach their boundary.
The arrogant person turns his side to lead others away from God's way and is promised the burning punishment, opposing the yielding turn toward a rider.
God could fix people in their places so they could neither proceed nor return, showing that even the ability to move along a route is bestowed.
The chargers penetrate into the midst of the gathering, completing the horse sequence with fast, directed arrival rather than hesitant footing.
Hearts become harder than stone even though stones split, release water, or fall in fear of God; this resistant hardness reverses the section's softened human-animal response.
A chest opened to submission and light is set against hearts hardened toward God's remembrance, defining the human resistance opposite the softened mount.
Valuable pregnant camels are abandoned at the Hour, overturning ordinary ownership and reliance on the useful animal.
Tethered horses are kept ready as organized power, a trained and prepared animal condition set against the unbroken camel of the section.
No bearer of burdens bears another's moral burden, a boundary against transferring the load even though a mount physically carries its rider.
The repeated rule that no burden-bearer bears another's burden marks the moral limit of the section's carrying image.
A heavily laden soul cannot have its load carried even by close kin, sharpening the boundary between bodily transport and accountable burden.
No burden-bearer bears another's burden before return to the Lord, setting individual return against reliance on another carrier.
The scripture's rule that no bearer bears another's burden supplies another explicit boundary for the mount-and-load image.
The Day is called a difficult day, giving eschatological content to the ʿusr toward which the resistant person is eased.
That difficult Day is expressly not easy for disbelievers, placing yusr and its negation around the denier's destination.
God's enemies are gathered toward the Fire and marshaled together, an imposed procession opposite being conducted away from it.
God makes the earth a cradle and threads roads through it so people may find guidance, another formulation of terrain prepared for passage.
Broad passageways are placed through the earth so people may be guided, turning resistant terrain into traversable routes.
When apparently trapped on the journey, Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him, placing confidence in the route's divine guide.
Setting out toward Midian, Moses hopes his Lord will guide him to the right way, a travel prayer for direction.
Believers are called to let their hearts humble to remembrance rather than become hardened, developing the human yielding behind the softened-animal comparison.
Unperceiving humans are compared to livestock and called still further astray, another animal comparison in which failure of guidance is decisive.
Misleaders bear their own full burdens and part of the burdens of those they mislead, joining following with the weight produced by bad direction.
God charges no soul beyond its capacity, another limit supporting the section's image of a bearer fitted rather than injured by its load.
Avoiding the major forbidden acts brings expiation and an honorable entrance, extending the ج ن ب family's deliberate separation from danger.
The believers are those who avoid major sins and indecencies, using the same root family for a practiced distance from harm.
Those who avoid major sins and indecencies enact the self-directed avoidance that the section distinguishes from being led away by God.
After revealed knowledge, no protecting ally or وَاقٍ exists against God, marking the limit of creaturely protection.
God saves those who believed and had taqwa from the destruction of Salih's opponents, making rescue the divine answer to caution.
God saves the believers who had taqwa from the punishing wind, another concrete event in which the cautious are delivered by Him.
Ships like landmarks on the sea are counted among God's signs, identifying the conveyances whose motion He can stop in the next ayah.
After the ark's rescue formula, Noah is told to ask his Lord for a blessed landing, placing arrival as well as carriage under divine care.
Ships that run through the sea with what benefits people are among God's signs, another useful conveyance sustained within His ordering.
God sends winds so ships may sail by His command and people may seek His bounty and give thanks, linking motion to gift and gratitude.
Pilgrims remember God's name over the livestock He provided and feed the needy from them, placing animal provision inside remembrance and giving.
The Lord promises to give until the addressee is satisfied, reversing the direction of human أَعْطَى and locating final sufficiency in the divine giver.
God creates creatures with distinct modes of movement, including those walking on four legs, grounding the section's attention to animal gait in created form.
Animal skins become dwellings found light on travel days, extending livestock's bestowed usefulness from carrying to portable travel equipment.
